correctness.rationale: At b>0, a>2sqrt(b), r=(a-sqrt(a²-4b))/2>0 is the lower equilibrium with ar=r²+b and a>2r; det of the Jacobian at (r,r²) is eps*r*(2r-a)<0. The backward left stable branch stays in 0<x<r,mu>r² since xdot>0 and mudot=-eps(mu+b-ax)<0 there; it cannot blow up at finite backward time and reaches every higher horizontal section exactly once. Inverse graph ODE bounds 0<=mu_eps(eta)-r²<=a eps/r log(r/eta). Along fixed section, log derivative gives -eps log x(mu0) as integral of (mu-x²)/(mu+b-ax), whose difference from mu/(mu+b) is O(eta) uniformly on x<=eta; first eps->0 then eta->0 gives action integral [mu-r²-b log((mu+b)/(r²+b))]. Subtracting two fixed-section limits cancels the lower endpoint and a-dependent r, giving independent-of-a attenuation. Independent numerical stable-branch integrations at eps=.12,.05,.02 show convergence of action at mu=2,5 for a=3,b=2; only analytical argument proves limit.
